context_requirements: Functional thymidine salvage pathways (TK1) to modulate sensitivity
Intact p53 pathway for robust transcriptional DNA damage response
Adequate folate transport and polyglutamylation for classical antifolates (less relevant for non-classical inhibitors)
falsifiers: No decrease in S-phase or proliferation markers (e.g., CCNA2, CCNB1, CDK1) at 24 h in any responsive line
No induction of p53 targets (CDKN1A, GADD45A) at 6 or 24 h
Complete absence of transcriptional response in all nine lines
Thymidine rescue abolishes all transcriptional changes (would confirm TS as sole target, but absence of rescue would suggest off-target effects)

evidence.supports: TS inhibition causes translational derepression and increased TS protein levels without changes in mRNA
TS inhibitors cause S-phase arrest and growth inhibition in human and murine cell lines
TS inhibition combined with DNA damage leads to S-phase slowdown and cell death
TS siRNA suppresses TS expression and restores chemosensitivity to TS inhibitors
NF-kB activity is upregulated in TS inhibitor-resistant cells and may antagonize apoptosis
